R01.note: Strong ACL pre-filter, ingestion and permission CI gate, but no ACL-change propagation or bound, no outage behaviour, no owner-written gold set or pass bar, and no cost/latency estimate.

R02.note: Solid core with a per-team leak gate and feedback into the golden set, but no parse-failure reporting, no exact-term justification for hybrid, no ACL-change bound, and no pass bar or cost estimate.

R03.note: Thorough and well-gated plan with visible failures and pass thresholds, missing an explicit doc-ACL staleness bound, outage behaviour, who reads logs, and a cost/latency estimate.

R04.note: Hourly ACL re-sync and a concrete pass bar are good, but deletions, parse-failure listing, outage behaviour and a cost estimate are missing.

R05.note: Best on revocation bound and cache/log side channels, but no SSO/IdP group resolution, no reranker or top-k, no pass bar, and feedback does not feed the gold set.

R06.note: Very complete with minutes-level revocation and loud parse failures, but citations lack explicit links, no outage behaviour, log readers unstated, and no cost/latency estimate.

R07.note: Clean pre-filter and retrieval, but omits prompt injection and side channels, parse-failure handling, ACL-change bound, and an automated per-change permission gate.

R08.note: Strong ingestion and permission sync with a 15-minute bound and fail-closed groups, but no explicit prompt-injection defence, no pass bar, no content owner, and no cost estimate.

R09.note: The most complete plan, but it has no outage behaviour, does not say who reads the logs, gives no cost/latency estimate, and runs somewhat long.

R10.note: Compact but thin: no SSO groups, no staleness bound, no hash-based refresh or parse-failure handling, no injection defence, and the permission tests are underspecified.
